title: Ideal-square intersection for an H1-regular quotient
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $I\subseteq J$ ideals of $A$. Suppose there are $g_1,\ldots,g_r\in J$, $r\geq0$, whose images in $A/I$ generate $J/I$ and are an $H_1$-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]: the first homology of their Koszul complex over $A/I$ vanishes. Then
$$I\cap J^2=IJ.$$
There is no Noetherian, local, proper-ideal, or nonzero-ring hypothesis, and the empty sequence is allowed.

source.place: Tag 0666 (lemma-conormal-sequence-H1-regular), full statement, used in divisors.tex Tag 063N (lemma-transitivity-conormal-quasi-regular).

proof.text: Put $G=(g_1,\ldots,g_r)$. Since $g_i\in J$ and their images generate $J/I$, we have $G\subseteq J$ and $J=I+G$: for $j\in J$, write its image as $\bar j=\sum_i\bar c_i\bar g_i$, lift each coefficient to $c_i\in A$, and obtain $j-\sum_i c_ig_i\in I$. Expanding finite sums of products of elements of $J=I+G$ now gives $J^2=I^2+IG+G^2$. Hence every $x\in I\cap J^2$ has an expression $x=a+b+c$ with $a\in I^2$, $b\in IG$, $c\in G^2$.

For such an $x$, $I^2\subseteq I$ and $IG\subseteq I$, so $c=x-a-b\in I$; also $G^2\subseteq G$, so $c\in I\cap G$. Apply [lem-sfb-h1-regular-generator-ideal-intersection] to the given ring $A$, ideal $I$, and precisely the lifted sequence $g_1,\ldots,g_r$: the needed $H_1$-regularity in $A/I$ is an assumption of this item. It yields $I\cap G=IG$, hence $c\in IG$. Since $I\subseteq J$ and $G\subseteq J$, all of $a\in I^2$, $b\in IG$, and $c\in IG$ lie in $IJ$. Thus $x\in IJ$ and $I\cap J^2\subseteq IJ$.

Conversely, each product $ij$ with $i\in I$ and $j\in J$ belongs to $I$ because $I$ is an ideal, and to $J^2$ because $I\subseteq J$. Finite sums give $IJ\subseteq I\cap J^2$, proving equality. If $r=0$, generation says $J=I$ and the identity is $I\cap I^2=I^2$; the same expansion has $G=0$. If $I=A$, then $J=A$ and both sides are $A$, including the zero ring. No step uses a properness or finiteness condition on the ring.
